newsitem.title: USA: N.C. House sends rental car tax back to committee.
newsitem.headline: N.C. House sends rental car tax back to committee.

text.p: A bill allowing North Carolina municipalities to fund mass transit programs with car rental taxes was sent back to a House committee Tuesday amid complaints from car rental firms.

The House had been scheduled to vote on the bill (HB1231) but instead re-referred it to the House Finance Committee, a House clerk said. The move means the bill could be revised or returned to the floor as is for a vote.
The bill would allow regional transit authorities to levy a 5 percent tax on rental cars to fund mass transit programs.
In Durham, Orange and Wake counties, the Triangle Transit Authority hopes to use the tax to finance a light rail system in the Raleigh-Durham-Chapel Hill triangle area.
The authority is also seeking federal funding for the proposed system, which would be financed with tax-exempt bonds.
Owners of car rental firms and members of the Car And Truck Rental And Leasing Association rallied outside the Capital Tuesday to protest the tax.
"It's an ugly tax," said Nancy Workman, co-owner of a Thrifty Rental Car franchise in Raleigh. "This is a tax to fund something that ultimately would make it so people don't need rental cars."
She said car rental firms had been singled out because lawmakers mistakenly believe the tax would be paid by tourists and not local residents.
"In fact, well over 50 percent of the rental car business in the three counties is local business," Workman said.
The tax would come on top of the 8 percent highway use tax that car rental customers already pay.

Car rental taxes are an increasingly popular source of revenue for local governments. Atlanta, Detroit, Phoenix, Seattle and Tuscon already levy them to fund sports arenas, according to the Travel Industry Association of America.
